readings.title: A repair with two outcomes
readings.instruction: Read the original simulation passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: At Maple Repair Circle, a volunteer helped Sam mend a torn backpack strap. Sam expected the volunteer to do the sewing while he waited. Instead, she demonstrated the first stitches and asked him to continue. The repair took longer than a professional service would have taken. Yet Sam left with a usable bag and enough confidence to mend a smaller tear at home. The circle did not claim to replace paid repair businesses. Its aim was to make simple skills less mysterious, while referring unsafe or highly specialised jobs to people qualified to handle them.
knowledgePoints: 阅读：主旨、细节、推断与语境词义

readings.title: The part nobody could find
readings.instruction: Read the original simulation passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: A café owned a useful mixer whose small plastic control knob had broken. A replacement machine was easy to order, but a replacement knob was not listed in the supplier's catalogue. The manager contacted a repair shop, which found a compatible part after checking the model. The mixer returned to service at a modest cost. The experience led the café to ask about spare parts before buying other equipment. Purchase price remained important, but it no longer stood alone. The ability to maintain a machine could affect its cost over several years.

readings.title: Labels at the repair table
readings.instruction: Read the original simulation passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: A repair event once used a single queue for every object. Visitors with loose buttons waited behind people discussing complicated electrical faults. Volunteers introduced coloured cards indicating sewing, simple mechanical work and assessment by an electrical specialist. The cards did not guarantee that an object could be repaired. They helped direct it to someone able to assess the task. Waiting times became easier to estimate, and visitors could decide whether to stay. Organisers stressed that a quick assessment was not a safety certificate. Clear categories improved the event without making promises beyond the volunteers' skills.
knowledgePoints: 阅读：主旨、细节、推断与语境词义

readings.title: Keeping a bicycle log
readings.instruction: Read the original simulation passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: After replacing two worn tyres in one month, Lina started recording her bicycle maintenance. The log showed that both failures followed rides with heavily loaded bags, and she realised she rarely checked tyre pressure. A mechanic explained the recommended pressure range and how loading affected handling. Lina began checking before longer trips. She could not conclude that pressure had caused every previous problem, because the roads and tyres also varied. Still, the record helped her ask a more informed question. She kept the log brief so that maintaining it did not become another task she would avoid.
knowledgePoints: 阅读：主旨、细节、推断与语境词义

translation.stem:
Translate the following original passage into Chinese. Preserve the meaning and logical relationships.

Repairing an object often teaches us how it works. It can also change the way we think about buying a replacement. Not everything can be repaired safely at home, however. Knowing when to ask a skilled person for help is part of being a responsible consumer.
translation.referenceAnswer: 修理一件物品往往能让我们了解它的工作原理，也能改变我们购买替代品时的想法。不过，并不是所有东西都能在家中安全修好。懂得何时向有技能的人寻求帮助，也是负责任消费的一部分。
translation.explanation: 参考译文仅示范一种表达。评分时关注信息完整性、转折和条件等逻辑关系；意思准确且中文自然的其他译法同样有效。

writing.stem:
Write an English response of about 120 words to the following original simulation task. Use your own examples and organise your ideas clearly.

Explain whether neighbourhood repair events deserve support. Give a concrete example and address a safety concern.
writing.sampleAnswer: Neighbourhood repair events deserve support because they can reduce waste while helping people learn. A person who mends a loose backpack strap with guidance may later feel able to repair a small tear independently. Such learning gives the event value beyond the object saved. However, enthusiasm cannot replace technical competence. Electrical equipment, in particular, should be assessed only by someone with appropriate skills. Organisers should explain the limits of the service and refer unsuitable jobs to qualified businesses. A simple booking system could direct each item to the right volunteer. I would begin with sewing and basic bicycle care, where safe demonstrations are possible. A repair event works best when it combines practical participation with honest limits.
writing.explanation: 范文供完成作答后对照。允许不同立场与例子；围绕题目要求论述清楚、理由充分、语言准确即可。

criteria.name: 任务完成与内容
criteria.description: 回应题目所有要求，观点明确，包含相关理由、具体例子或可行建议。

criteria.name: 组织与衔接
criteria.description: 结构清楚，信息顺序合理，句段衔接自然，格式符合写作目的。

criteria.name: 语言与表达
criteria.description: 词汇使用恰当，句式基本准确，表达清晰；错误按其对理解的影响扣分。

knowledgePoints: 英语写作：观点、建议与应用文
